source.title: Identifying Interpretable Visual Features in Artificial and Biological Neural Systems
source.authors: David A. Klindt; S. Sanborn; Francisco Acosta; Frédéric Poitevin; N. Miolane

record.tranche_reason: The study explicitly tests whether non-axis-aligned activation-space directions are more interpretable than individual units, using K-means and interpretability measures rather than the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results comparing K-means directions with individual neurons or units, including in-silico psychophysics and pairwise additions. It also reports that K does not impact the tested results. Human-versus-in-silico psychophysics validation results are not rows because they validate the metric rather than test the direction-versus-unit claim. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests the superposition hypothesis in a new setting: a CIFAR-10 ResNet50 layer and macaque/human visual data. It asks whether K-means directions, not aligned with neurons, are more interpretable than single units. No listed version covers this system. V4 names LLMs. V6 needs a 1-D vs multi-D comparison, which the study never makes, since K-means centroids are 1-D by construction. So the results go under fits_no_version rather than under version verdicts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find non-axis-aligned directions in a CNN and in visual cortex data that are more interpretable than single units. They call this consistent with superposition and suggest the brain may use it. They also report feature synergy and links to disentanglement, and say better metrics and feature-finding methods are needed. The interpretability metric was validated only for early layers.
record.recipe_differences: Uses K-means and an MEI-based interpretability index or in-silico psychophysics on trained CNN activations and biological visual-response data; it does not use the original toy-model sparse-feature optimization and geometry analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The interpretability metric's agreement with human judgments is better for early ResNet50 layers; psychophysics difficulty and semantic metric vary; K did not affect the reported direction advantage in the tested range; training shifts predictability from low-level color toward high-level labels.

fits_no_version.finding: In a CIFAR-10 ResNet50 layer, K-means directions not aligned with neurons have higher II and in-silico psychophysics accuracy than individual neurons. The gain is largest for color and present even at initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision CNNs contain non-neuron-aligned activation directions more interpretable than single neurons (vision analogue of V4).

fits_no_version.finding: In macaque IT, macaque AM, and human fMRI data, K-means activity clusters are more interpretable than single units or voxels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Biological visual cortex encodes interpretable features along non-axis-aligned population directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Some neuron pairs, when summed, are more interpretable than either neuron alone, though most pairings reduce II.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse neuron combinations can yield more interpretable features than their constituents.

fits_no_version.finding: K-means features are sparser across the image manifold than neuron activations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More interpretable features are more sparsely active on the data manifold.

record.problems: The interpretability index is a proxy and its validation against human judgments is stronger for early layers. Many direction-versus-unit results are presented in figures without exact values in the text. The study does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional feature representations.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity-dependent transition, or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of polysemanticity without capacity pressure. The untrained-model gap (r5) is suggestive but not framed this way.
No LLMs. The analogous result is in vision CNNs and cortex only.
No completeness, stability, or canonicity tests of SAE features. The SAE is used only as an interpretability baseline.
No comparison of 1-D directions with multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Clusters transfer across fMRI subjects and scan sessions better than voxels (universality/drift).
Neurons more co-active with the population have lower II (privileged-basis argument).
K-means features score higher than neurons on disentanglement metrics (DCI, MCC) in AM data.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 linkage is unsupported. K-means centroids are 1-D by construction, and no multi-D alternative is tested. Evidence for superposition here is indirect: interpretability of mixed directions. There is no test of more features than dimensions; K=512 > N=256 did not change II. The untrained-model gap means interpretable directions may not reflect learned superposition. Analysis is restricted to layer 1 because the metric is valid only for early layers.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test small toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Studies visual CNNs and biological visual responses, not LLMs or LLM feature recovery.
The sparse-autoencoder comparison concerns interpretability scores; it does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Finds interpretable one-dimensional directions, but does not establish that underlying features are exclusively one-dimensional or compare them directly with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: ResNet50 pre-trained on CIFAR-10
rows.size_stated: N = 256 neurons in the analyzed layer
rows.operation_detail: Compared interpretability-index distributions for individual neurons and directions found by K-means.
rows.measure: Interpretability Index (II), based on pairwise similarity of top MEIs
rows.baseline: Individual neurons; other baselines include PCA, ICA, NMF, and a sparse autoencoder.
rows.value: K-means directions have higher II than individual neurons and all baselines; reported mean = −0.0159, compared with the sparse autoencoder's best mean = −0.0188.
rows.note: The paper reports no impact of K on II in the tested range. The comparison supports the greater interpretability of the identified directions, not the completeness or canonicality of any feature dictionary.
rows.check: Linked to V6 wrongly; no 1-D vs multi-D comparison exists. The SAE/PCA/ICA/NMF part of the baseline is the study's own method against alternatives and should not count as evidence. Only the neuron-vs-direction II gap bears on the hypothesis.

rows.subject: ResNet50 pre-trained on CIFAR-10
rows.size_stated: N = 256 neurons in the analyzed layer
rows.operation_detail: Compared in-silico psychophysics accuracy for K-means directions and individual neurons.
rows.value: K-means directions are more predictable than individual neurons across tested task difficulties; exact values figure only.
rows.note: The text reports the direction-versus-neuron result across low-, mid-, and high-level semantics and task difficulties.
rows.check: Not V6. Vision CNN, not LLM, so not V4. Paper says the gain is largest for the color metric.

rows.value: K-means directions are more predictable than individual neurons across tested task difficulties; exact values figure only.

rows.check: Not V6. Paper says the improvement shrinks toward label-level semantics, so this is the smallest gain.

rows.subject: Untrained and trained ResNet50 on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared in-silico psychophysics for neurons and activity clusters in untrained and trained models.
rows.value: The interpretability gap between neurons and activity clusters is already present at initialization; semantics shift from low-level color prediction in the untrained model toward high-level label information in the trained model.
rows.note: The gap is reported for clusters versus neurons; training changes the semantic level at which they are predictable.
rows.check: Not V6. The locator Appendix H is correct; the main text wrongly cites Appendix G. The gap is present at initialization, so it may reflect data or architecture rather than learned superposition.

rows.subject: ResNet50 pre-trained on CIFAR-10
rows.size_stated: N = 256 neurons in the analyzed layer
rows.operation_detail: Added pairs of z-scored neuron activities and compared their II with the maximum II of either neuron alone.

conditions.value: all pairs of neurons in the layer

rows.measure: Synergy, defined as II(a + b) − max[II(a), II(b)]
rows.baseline: The maximum individual II of the two neurons
rows.value: Most pairings reduce interpretability, but a good fraction of added pairs become more interpretable than either neuron alone.
rows.note: The paper does not give a numerical fraction in the text.
rows.check: Not V6. Synergy measures neuron-pair combinations, not feature dimensionality. Most pairs reduce II; no fraction is given.

rows.subject: Vinken et al. (2023) macaque inferior temporal cortex dataset
rows.operation_detail: Compared K-means activation clusters with individual units using in-silico psychophysics.

conditions.value: color, LPIPS, and three image-condition labels

rows.value: Clusters show the same, if not a larger, increase in interpretability than the directions found in the CNN analysis; exact values figure only.
rows.note: The paper describes interpretable clusters involving multiple IT neurons.
rows.check: Biological data (macaque IT), not an artificial model; no listed version applies.

rows.subject: Higgins et al. (2021) anterior middle macaque face-area dataset
rows.size_stated: 159 neurons; 2100 human and monkey face images
rows.operation_detail: Compared K-means activation clusters with individual units using in-silico psychophysics.

conditions.value: brightness and LPIPS; no label-based metric

rows.value: K-means features have higher psychophysics performance than individual neurons across tested difficulty levels; exact values figure only.
rows.note: The paper also reports that these features score higher on the reported disentanglement measures, but that measure is not included here because it does not measure the dimensionality claim.
rows.check: Biological data (macaque AM); no listed version applies.

rows.subject: Allen et al. (2022) human fMRI visual-response dataset
rows.operation_detail: Compared psychophysics accuracy for K-means activity clusters and fMRI units.
rows.value: Clusters achieve higher psychophysics accuracy than units in all analyzed brain areas; exact values figure only.
rows.note: The paper describes fMRI voxels as potentially already being linear combinations of neurons.
rows.check: Human fMRI voxels, which are already mixtures of neurons; no listed version applies.

rows.subject: ResNet50 pre-trained on CIFAR-10
rows.size_stated: N = 256 neurons and K = 256 K-means features
rows.operation_detail: Compared the distribution of MEIs on an image-manifold embedding for neurons and K-means features.
rows.measure: Sparsity of activations across the natural-image manifold
rows.value: K-means features are much sparser on the manifold than neural activations.
rows.note: This is sparsity across the image manifold, not a test of sparse co-activation under capacity pressure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet50 on CIFAR-10, analyzed layer; macaque IT and AM datasets; and human fMRI clusters in Subject 1
reader_labels.reason: The identified activation-space directions or clusters are more interpretable than individual units by II or in-silico psychophysics (r1-r5, r7-r9); some pairwise neuron additions also improve interpretability (r6).
